key_insight: Physics-informed Vision Transformer frameworks estimate diffuse horizontal irradiance from scarce sky images, approaching the accuracy of a model trained on the complete dataset.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce reliance on costly irradiance sensors for photovoltaic performance assessment and solar energy forecasting.
method: Add calculated extraterrestrial irradiance and cyclic time encodings.
Predict synthetic global horizontal irradiance, then use it to refine diffuse irradiance estimates.
Process raw and cloud-overlay sky images in parallel using unsupervised, physics-informed segmentation.
evidence_signal: At Chilbolton Observatory, single-month training and temporally disjoint full-year testing yielded RMSE differences from a full-data ViT of 2–3 W/m² for the sequential framework and 1–6 W/m² for the dual-parallel framework.
watch_item: Validation at one temperate-climate site leaves transferability to other climates and sky-camera setups uncertain.
paper_title: Vision Transformers for Estimating Irradiance Using Data Scarce Sky Images
